summary: Patch adds ensure_ascii=False to json.dumps(not self.is_required) in AutocompleteMixin, but that argument is a boolean whose serialization never contains non-ASCII characters, so the change has zero effect on the reported JSONField unicode display bug. Wrong location entirely — real fix belongs in JSONField.prepare_value (django/forms/fields.py), not the admin autocomplete widget.

issues.description: Issue not resolved. Bug is about JSONField admin display escaping unicode (e.g. 中国 -> \u4e2d\u56fd). Patch touches AutocompleteMixin's data-allow-clear which serializes a bool (not self.is_required); json.dumps(True/False) yields 'true'/'false' — no unicode ever. Real JSONField widget/prepare_value path untouched.

Incorrect approach/wrong location. ensure_ascii=False on boolean serialization is meaningless. Correct fix is in django/forms/fields.py JSONField.prepare_value (or the field's bound_data), where actual JSON string values are dumped.
Change looks special-cased to pass a repro test that only checks the string 'ensure_ascii=False' appears, rather than actually correcting unicode handling in JSONFields.
